restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

No advice: every phase runs inside the algorithm and the claimed time is the sum of hard budgets (proof 2, 6): P at its counted bound (exact node and leaf counts recomputed by r5-trail-0..3 and capped by counters; T3 leaf at 2^8 >= the counted 194.5; full w1 evaluations capped at 2^30 and charged at 2^12): 2^37.9678 units; B' at 2^34 units plus at most one update (< 2^13); at most 2^16 connector attempts of at most 2^18 work units; K = 112 spaces of 2^32 pairs at most 429 primitives each (worst path of the counted FES early-abort program, r5-ecount); FES tables 2^18 primitives per space; at most 2^11 stage-2 pairs per space. Total 2^38.6805, claimed 38.77. No expected value is charged.

Development runs are not charged and are disclosed (proof 0): they fixed the six B' design constants R = 16, DMIN = 40 and the weights KW = 1.0, MW = 0.25, LB = 1.0, PREF = 1.0 (75 processes, 1,559 CPU-s with the steering check in v7's ledger); some used the published difference of Guo et al. as a test case. Uncharged v5 runs also set the connector's DMIN = 33 (the least DF for which E's window exists) and its 2^18 work-unit cap (charged in full, never bound). These are the only constants fixed by uncharged runs; trail2c's c1max = 30 filter never applies. This reverses v7's statement that the B' constants were charged with a machine-capacity window. Every success rate used comes from runs made after the constants were fixed: the v6 full-scale run and pre-registrations A and B. Sensitivity, not claimed: charging B''s development (1,559 CPU-s at 2^38 primitives per core-second) gives 39.62, v7's whole development ledger (12,527 CPU-s) 41.48, v7's window 44.25.

Probability space: fresh algorithmic coins, fixed target, no advice. Success >= 1 - 0.00043 - 2^-29 - 2^-155 - (1 - 0.013)^112 - 2^-12 > 0.76 under H1 (for each advice B' can output, per accepted space E outputs a pair with probability >= 0.013), H2 (B' candidates), H3 (connector acceptance of B' outputs) and H4 (the trail search stays under its full-evaluation cap); claimed 0.40, which needs s >= 0.0046 for the final advice. E's FES stage 1 computes exactly the values of the v8 stage 1 (a quadratic-map identity, proof 2.4), so E's outputs and H1 are unchanged.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): the pre-registered v6 full-scale run (14 collisions in 512 spaces; denominator and numerator re-executed by r5-den-0..2 and r5-replay); pre-registration A: nine B' runs under the shipped program and budget (all outputs, 2^23.4-2^28.2 units) each followed by 128 connector attempts (45-120 accepted); pre-registration B: E on 2 spaces per advice (round-2 passes 1.033 x the trail value; 3 collisions with fresh advice, replayed by r5-replay8). r5-trail-0..3 recompute every count of P; r5-ecount executes the counted v8 and FES stage-1 programs, FES exactness checks on full 2^10-point windows, and one counted T3 pass of P; r5-bp-0..4 re-derive every B' output and run 288 organizer-seeded connector attempts; r5-bpfull executes B' whole with its budget counter.

E's stage 1 tests the round-2 rows in the early-abort order of Th0rgal 7deb1595 (row 66, then row 81), credited; Th0rgal is a co-author. Memory: largest measured peak of any phase 113.5 MB (B'); declared 30.

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the counted early-abort E with fast exhaustive search of the quadratic round-1 input (after Bouillaguet et al., CHES 2010) and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: For each advice (beta1', beta0') that B' can output and one connector attempt with fresh coins that is accepted on it, the enumeration E (proof 2.4) on its 2^32-pair window outputs a pair (all 24 round-2 equations hold and the 256-bit digests are equal) with probability at least s0 = 0.013, and the stage-2 cap of 2^11 pairs per space does not bind. This is a bound per advice, not an average over advices.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability: given the final advice, the K = 112 accepted spaces are i.i.d. (independent coins), so Pr[no output] = (1 - s)^112 <= 0.2310; the claimed 0.40 needs s >= 0.0046 for the final advice. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1. E's FES stage 1 outputs exactly what the v8 stage 1 output on every space (proof 2.4), so the measurements behind H1 apply unchanged.
heuristics.extrapolation: Pre-registered v6 full-scale run with the advice that the shipped B' reproduces from LABEL_B within its budget (k = 0; r5-bp-0): E output a pair in 14 of the first 512 accepted spaces (s-hat = 0.0273; one-sided 99% Clopper-Pearson lower bound 0.0133 >= s0); r5-den-0..2 re-run all 538 attempt indices up to the 512th accepted one (the whole denominator) and r5-replay re-derives the 14 positives. Across advice (Markov premise: E depends on the advice only through the exact 2-round difference alpha2, which every advice reaches): pre-registration B enumerated 2 spaces of each of the 9 advices of pre-registration A: 4,760 round-2 passes against 4,608 expected (ratio 1.033, per advice 0.975-1.125), and 3 collisions in 16 spaces of fresh advice (k = 4 and 7), replayed by r5-replay8. Largest stage-2 count per space: 307 (E check) and 301 (v6), against the cap 2,048. Sampling premise: SHAKE-256-expanded coins from distinct seeds give the same per-attempt probabilities as fresh coins.
heuristics.limitations: s0 is measured on one advice; for the other advice only round-2 rates and 3 collisions are measured. Those show more variation than an independent-pair model predicts, all upward: pooled round-2 ratio 1.033 (2.2 Poisson standard deviations above 1, inside the pre-registered 99% interval), advice 4 2.8 above; 3 collisions in 16 fresh spaces (probability about 0.01 at the v6 rate), two of them in one space (about 0.007); s counts spaces with at least one collision. The v6 run had a disclosed decision rule (submit if s0 >= 0.002), the outcome-selection premise reviewers flagged for v7; the factor 2.8 between s0 and the needed 0.0046 is the margin (3.3 at K = 128). The organizer seeds are public and the harness draws no inference.

heuristics.statement: B' candidates with fresh coins are independent; each yields an accepted advice with probability at least q_c0 = 0.0742 and costs at most 2^26.85 units (twice the largest observed candidate).
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability: with H3, at least floor(2^34 / 2^26.85) = 142 candidates fit B''s budget, so Pr[B' exhausts its budget before a good advice] <= (1 - 0.0742 x (1 - 0.2831))^142 = 0.00043, including restarts. The time cap does not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Pre-registration A (proof 4.2): nine B' runs (k = 0: LABEL_B; k = 1..8: new labels) under the shipped program and budget, started together, none stopped or repeated: 65 candidates, 9 accepted (q_c-hat = 0.138; one-sided 95% CP lower bound 0.0742); largest candidate 2^25.848 units; whole runs 2^23.4-2^28.2 units. r5-bp-0..4 re-derive every output from its label at the logged counts and audit one other logged attempt each; r5-bpfull executes run k = 1 whole (counted cost equal to the log) and stops B' at a 2^20-unit budget.
heuristics.limitations: Nine runs; the per-candidate cost is bounded by observation, not by a cap. Sensitivity: a Markov bound from the mean run cost (2^27.11 units) gives 0.0084 instead of 0.00043; success stays > 0.80.

heuristics.statement: An advice output by B' has connector acceptance probability q >= 0.10 per attempt with fresh coins, except with probability at most f_up = 0.2831 over B''s coins.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability: a good advice gives 112 accepted attempts within 2^12 except with probability < 2^-155 (Chernoff, mean >= 409.6); weak advice is discarded and B' resumes, so H3 enters as f_up^16 < 2^-29 (at most 16 advice rounds) and through H2's bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: Pre-registration A: 128 attempts with each of the 9 advices: 120, 105, 68, 93, 104, 83, 58, 68, 45 accepted (744 of 1,152, all verified); every 99% Clopper-Pearson lower bound is >= 0.255, so all 9 are good and f_up is the one-sided 95% upper bound of 0/9. Organizer-seeded attempts in r5-bp-0..4: 196 of 288 accepted and verified with the public seed (consistent with q >= 0.10 for each advice).
heuristics.limitations: Nine advices; f_up is a 95% bound. Acceptance varies between advices (0.35-0.94), which is why the restart rule exists.

heuristics.statement: The v11 trail-search stage T3 (per-core pruning threshold; no shared state enters any count) performs at most FCAP = 2^30 full w1 evaluations in total over the 467 kept cores.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability: if it failed, P would stop at FCAP and the run would output nothing. F is a fixed number of a deterministic program, so H4 holds on every run or on none. The time bound charges FCAP x 2^12 primitives in full and does not depend on H4.
heuristics.extrapolation: The shipped v11 T3 was run on the first 108 of the 467 kept cores in its own order (23.3% of the 1,379,275,399,350 leaves), including the output core (w1 = 127, w2 = 24, the same beta2, 155 full evaluations): F = 324,445 over these cores, largest per-core count 71,740. FCAP is exceeded only if the remaining 359 cores average more than 2,990,020 full evaluations each, 41.7 times the largest per-core count observed.
heuristics.limitations: A partial run: 359 cores (76.7% of the leaves) were not run to completion with the per-core threshold. The count is not re-executed by the organizer (as for the full T3 minimisation of 113fc83). GordoAR (bc0f7b5) introduced a heuristic of this kind for the earlier, schedule-dependent form.
